preconditions.description: The integer n (length of genome) is between 4 and 255 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(s) == n and all(c in {'A', 'C', 'G', 'T', '?'} for c in s)
preconditions.description: The string s has length n and consists only of 'A', 'C', 'G', 'T', or '?' characters.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '===' or (len(stdout) == n and all(c in {'A', 'C', 'G', 'T'} for c in stdout))
postconditions.description: If decoding is impossible, stdout is '==='. Otherwise, stdout is a valid genome of length n with no '?' characters.

postconditions.expression: stdout != '===' and (lambda s: all(s.count(c) == n // 4 for c in {'A', 'C', 'G', 'T'}))(stdout)
postconditions.description: If stdout is not '===', then the counts of 'A', 'C', 'G', and 'T' in stdout are exactly equal (n must be divisible by 4).

postconditions.expression: stdout != '===' and (lambda s: all(s[i] == s[i] for i in range(n)))
postconditions.description: If stdout is not '===', it is a valid replacement of all '?' in s with 'A', 'C', 'G', or 'T'.
